introduction: These short passages are addressed by Bahá’u’lláh and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to the Jewish people in the language of their own scripture: Sinai and the burning Tree, Zion and Carmel, the throne of David, the Friend and the One who conversed with God. They announce that what the prophets promised has come, and some of them reproach those who do not recognize it. The passages set beside them are mostly the promises themselves, from the Torah, the Psalms and the Prophets, so that the echoes can be heard. A few come from Jewish tradition and from elsewhere to state the other side of the conversation: the command not to add to the word, the rabbis' warning against calculating the end, Maimonides on how a Messiah is known, Paul's insistence that God has not cast away His people, and a Council's rejection of the old charge of collective guilt.
questions: Each address borrows the images of the Hebrew Bible. Which of the promises quoted beside the readings do you hear most clearly in them?
Deuteronomy forbids adding to the word and also gives a test for a true prophet. How would you expect a faithful Jewish reader to apply both to a new claim?
The Talmud counsels waiting and warns against announcing that the time has come. What is to be respected in that patience?
One reading addresses Jews as ready to crucify Jesus again. Reading it beside the Council's declaration and Shylock's speech, how do you think such language should be read and taught today?
Paul says God has not cast away His people. How can one religion announce fulfilment to another without contempt for it?

outside.why: Exodus tells how on the third day there were thunders and lightnings and a thick cloud upon the mount, and Moses spoke and God answered him by a voice.
Isaiah calls: O Zion, that bringest good tidings, get thee up into the high mountain; say unto the cities of Judah, Behold your God.
Isaiah foretells a rod out of the stem of Jesse, on whom the spirit of the Lord shall rest.
The psalm recalls the oath sworn to David concerning his throne, and says that the Lord hath chosen Zion for His habitation.

Hillel also put the whole Torah into one saying, and then added: the rest is its interpretation; go study. What is the relation between a single Word that sums up the law and the many words it sums up?
Ezekiel saw the glory of the God of Israel come from the way of the east, and the earth shined with His glory.
Isaiah speaks of a child on whose shoulder the government shall be, called Wonderful, Counsellor, The Prince of Peace.
Zechariah cries: rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; behold, thy King cometh unto thee, lowly, and riding upon an ass.
Through Amos God promises to bring again the captivity of Israel and to plant them upon their land.
Exodus says that the Lord spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend.
Moses commands in Deuteronomy: ye shall not add unto the word which I command you. How would a faithful reader of that verse weigh a call to take hold of something new?
Malachi hears: behold, I will send my messenger, and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple.
Habakkuk is told that the vision is yet for an appointed time: though it tarry, wait for it.

The Talmud warns against those who calculate the end of days, lest people say when the date passes that the Messiah will no longer come, and counsels waiting. How does that tradition hear the words, your appointed time hath been fulfilled?
Paul, himself an Israelite, asks: hath God cast away His people? and answers: God forbid. What follows for how a people is addressed who are said not to recognize what has come?

The Second Vatican Council declared that what happened in the passion of Christ cannot be charged against all the Jews then alive, nor against the Jews of today. How should a reader now receive an address that speaks to Jews as those who crucified Jesus?
Shakespeare's Shylock asks: hath not a Jew eyes, hands, organs, senses, affections, passions? What must anyone who addresses a people as a whole remember about each person in it?
Deuteronomy gives a test for one who speaks in the name of the Lord: if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, the Lord hath not spoken it.
Maimonides taught that one should not presume the Messianic king must work miracles and wonders. If signs are not the test, by what would a careful community recognize the one it awaits?
The psalm says: pray for the peace of Jerusalem; they shall prosper that love thee.
Isaiah sees all nations flowing to the mountain of the Lord, for out of Zion shall go forth the law.

exodus-thunders-and-lightnings.text: And it came to pass on the third day in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud; so that all the people that was in the camp trembled. And Moses brought forth the people out of the camp to meet with God; and they stood at the nether part of the mount. And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the Lord descended upon it in fire: and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mount quaked greatly. And when the voice of the trumpet sounded long, and waxed louder and louder, Moses spake, and God answered him by a voice

ezekiel-glory-from-the-east.text: And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east: and his voice was like a noise of many waters: and the earth shined with his glory

deuteronomy-if-the-thing-follow-not.text: And if thou say in thine heart, How shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken? When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken, but the prophet hath spoken it presumptuously: thou shalt not be afraid of him

romans-gifts-without-repentance.text: For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance

psalm-lord-hath-chosen-zion.text: The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them, their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore. For the Lord hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation

deuteronomy-not-because-ye-were-more.text: The Lord did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people: But because the Lord loved you, and because he would keep the oath which he had sworn unto your fathers, hath the Lord brought you out with a mighty hand, and redeemed you out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt

shakespeare-hath-not-a-jew-eyes.text: Hath / not a Jew eyes? hath not a Jew hands, organs, / dimensions, senses, affections, passions? fed with / the same food, hurt with the same weapons, subject / to the same diseases, healed by the same means, / warmed and cooled by the same winter and summer, as / a Christian is? If you prick us, do we not bleed? / if you tickle us, do we not laugh? if you poison / us, do we not die
shakespeare-hath-not-a-jew-eyes.author: William Shakespeare
